reconciliation: The 2x disagreement collapses once the sample split is applied: both bands are gross slices of different eras of the same series, not two different factors.

Pre-2007 HML ≈ +43 bp/month gross lies between the two bands; post-2007 HML ≈ -7 bp/month is negative. The long-run 1926-2024 average (band A, 25-42) already embeds post-2007 decay; band B (50-70) is a gross top-vs-bottom-quintile phrasing anchored in the pre-2007 era.
Router's own arithmetic takes 50-70 down to 30-40 bp/month after 15-20 bp/month turnover costs — still a pre-2007/gross-era number, not a number our costed construction can earn.

Our VLUE construction measures net 25.23 bp/month; implied gross ≈ 25.61 bp/month after only 0.38 bp/month cost drag (105 bp total over the window because the 0/1 signal changes position rarely). That reproduces the LOW END of band A (25-42) — i.e. the long-run average that already includes post-2007 decay — and matches the decayed-modern consensus (post-2007 HML -7 bp/month; big-stock 42 -> 4 bp/month). It reproduces band B (50-70) under no costing, and no post-cost number here clears the 36 bp/month cash hurdle.
which_construction_reproduces_our_number: None as a tradable edge. Our construction (VLUE: momentum-filtered value, monthly rebalance, next-day-open fill, 0/1 weight, costs charged on position changes, 2004-2026 window) sits at the low end of 25-42 bp/month gross and below the 36 bp/month cash hurdle net. It does not reproduce 50-70 bp/month gross.
verdict: B6 kill verdict stands unchanged: established=false. Value underperforms SPY buy-and-hold (7.06 vs 10.28%/yr) and cash (3.07 vs 4.32%/yr). Best-case gross (~25.6 bp/month) is below the 36 bp/month hurdle before financing or short borrow. The literature gap does not resurrect the value line.
